items.change: The party arrived in Brandonsford following a treasure map whose marked locations they did not recognize.
items.impact_basis: Beat_1 establishes the party's guiding pursuit and their arrival in unknown land, framing what they are doing.
items.lasting_basis: Beat_1 sets up the treasure hunt that remains unresolved and will drive later Sessions.

items.change: Reginald the frog warned that a trickster Clurichen comes from the riverbanks into town every night.
items.impact_basis: Beat_6 reveals a new nightly danger in town that the party had not known about.
items.lasting_basis: Beat_6's nightly creature plausibly ties to Quinn's vanishing ale and is likely to come up again.

items.change: Eric the Reeve offered 1000 gold for the dragon's body, though Sir Phidipaldi then insulted him and challenged him to a duel he declined.
items.impact_basis: Beats 16-19 give the party a major paid goal and sour relations with the bounty-giver, with added dragon details in beats 17, 26 and 27.
items.lasting_basis: Beat_16's bounty is an open main pursuit and beat_19's insult will color dealings with Eric.

items.change: Lady Hilda, a seasoned warrior, offered to join the party for pay against the dragon, and Sir Phidipaldi said they would return for her.
items.impact_basis: Beat_10 offers a potential capable ally for the dragon hunt.
items.lasting_basis: Beat_10's standing offer is likely to be taken up when the party pursues the bounty.

items.change: The party learned that Bentley's restocking shipment never arrived and that nothing has come into town in months.
items.impact_basis: Beats 14 and 30 reveal a town-wide supply mystery.
items.lasting_basis: The unexplained missing shipments in beats 14 and 30 are likely to resurface, possibly tied to the dragon.

items.change: Drop Dead Ned offered himself and his killer wasp for hire at 100 gold a week, and Dr. Uriah said he would think about it.
items.impact_basis: Beats 20-22 introduce a murderous potential hireling with a standing offer.
items.lasting_basis: Beat_22's undecided offer may come up again but no commitment was made.

items.change: Farmer Gill offered Dunk his mule Shamus for 100 gold, and Dunk stayed in the barn to consider trading work for it.
items.impact_basis: Beats 25 and 29 present a minor purchase offer still undecided.
items.lasting_basis: Beat_29 leaves the offer open, but it is a small matter of an ordinary animal.

items.change: Gill described Warwick the smith growing paranoid and piling up lucky charms, perhaps to ward off the potion seller Ingrid.
items.impact_basis: Beats 30 and 32 add an odd local detail without changing the party's situation.
items.lasting_basis: Beats 30 and 32 hint at a possible mystery that may or may not return.

items.change: The party learned Warwick displays a superb mithril chain shirt that he refuses to sell.
items.impact_basis: Beat_31 identifies a desirable item but no progress toward obtaining it.
items.lasting_basis: Beat_31's mithril shirt is a possible future goal for a party member.

items.change: Sir Phidipaldi agreed to stage a fake ale delivery for Quinn for 100 gold to catch whoever steals his stock each night.
items.impact_basis: Beats 36 and 37 create a paid agreement and a mystery about vanishing ale.
items.lasting_basis: Beat_37's agreed sting is owed and likely to be played out next Session.

items.change: Bentley banned fighting in his tavern and sent Sir Phidipaldi to spend the night at the Golden Egg.
items.impact_basis: Beat_23 separated Sir Phidipaldi from the party for the night and ended the quarrel with Eric.
items.lasting_basis: Beat_23's exile is mainly a one-night arrangement, though it led to the Quinn deal.

items.change: The party talked their way past a night watchman into Brandonsford and learned the town's layout.
items.impact_basis: Beats 2-4 give arrival and orientation details without altering the situation.
items.lasting_basis: Beats 2-4 are mostly setting details for the town.
items.encounter_basis: The gate arrival is logistics and colour; the map arrival is already covered by thread_1.

items.change: Dr. Uriah spoke with Reginald the frog, who warned of the Clurichen.
items.impact_basis: Beat_6 is the scene's only substantive content, a warning already captured by thread_2.
items.lasting_basis: Beat_6's warning may matter later, as in thread_2.
items.encounter_basis: The frog conversation's central result is the Clurichen warning, which thread_2 already tells.

items.change: At the Clumsy Fox the party gained the dragon bounty, met Hilda and Ned, and Sir Phidipaldi's duel challenge to Eric got him ejected.
items.impact_basis: Beats 10, 16, 19, 22 and 23 together set the party's main goal and several offers.
items.lasting_basis: The bounty, offers and soured relations from beats 16-23 carry forward.
items.encounter_basis: The tavern's central events are the bounty, the glove-slap and the ejection, already told by thread_3, thread_4, thread_6 and beat_23.

items.change: Dunk spent the night drinking with Farmer Gill, hearing the town's lore and gossip and considering buying his mule.
items.impact_basis: Beats 25-33 are a hospitality exchange yielding the Brandon legend, Gill's sons hunting the dragon, and Warwick gossip.
items.lasting_basis: Beats 26-27 and 30-32 provide context likely useful later, though the stay itself is one night.
items.encounter_basis: Dunk's hospitable night with Gill, sharing drink and his own unknown origins while hearing the Sir Brandon legend, is meaningful personal context not told by the mule or Warwick threads.

items.change: Exiled to the Golden Egg, Sir Phidipaldi struck a 100-gold deal with Quinn to stage a fake ale delivery.
items.impact_basis: Beats 36-37 create the agreement captured by thread_10.
items.lasting_basis: Beat_37's sting is owed next Session.
items.encounter_basis: The central interaction is the Quinn deal, which thread_10 already tells.
